proof_summary: If \(F_{33}\) is prime, then \(\varphi(F_{33})=2^{2^{33}}\), while every smaller positive candidate has totient too small (including the endpoint power of two), so \(F_{33}\) is minimal. If \(F_{33}\) is composite, even candidates below \(2^{2^{33}+1}\) are excluded by writing them as \(2^k d\) with \(d\) odd and bounding \(\varphi(d)<d\); an odd candidate would be squarefree with prime factors among \(2^{2^j}+1\) for \(j<33\), whose totient contributions multiply to at most \(2^{\sum_{j<33}2^j}=2^{2^{33}-1}\), contradicting the required divisibility, while the stated power of two itself has the required totient.
